topic: what a Friday release checklist really needs

grades.notes:
coverage: 5 atoms across 4 types (number x2, mechanism, limit, object): the risk, the answer, the form, the outcome
specificity: each atom carries a figure or a named thing: 70%, 5 to 9 items, 19 items in three pauses of 7, 7 and 5, 1.5% to 0.8% in 8 hospitals
sourced: every row names a published work: the Google SRE book introduction, Gawande ch. 6, the WHO checklist, Haynes et al. NEJM 2009
surprise: atom 4 is not about software at all: a surgical checklist built around three stops, which a release list can borrow

novelty: operator 1 (the cost of not) prices the missing stop with atom 1, where piece 1 borrowed the surgical form; similar reports the overlap
truth: roughly 70% of outages come from changes in a live system (Google SRE book, Introduction); the answers are rollouts, detection, rollback
relevance: a Friday list usually checks the code and the tests; the change itself is where the outage starts, so that is the stop it needs
intrigue: seven of ten is a large share, and the gap is where most Friday lists put no stop at all
tone: plain; it states the share as roughly 70% as the source does and does not warn or tell the reader what to do

coherence: transit-map lends lines and stations; the table layout sets the two causes as ruled rows and the comparison hook as the last row
feasibility: one page, local fonts (Outfit, Work Sans), own palette from palette.py, the drawing is two lines of solid stations
